chunks: Certainly, Allāh, the Glorified, the Sublime, has made His remembrance the light for hearts
which hear with its help despite deafness, see with its help despite blindness and become submissive with its help despite unruliness.
In all the periods and times when there were no prophets, there have been persons with whom Allāh, precious are His bounties,
whispered through their wits and spoke through their minds.
With the help of the bright awakening of their ears, eyes and hearts
they keep reminding others of the remembrance of the days of Allāh and making others feel fear for Him like guide-points in wildernesses.
Whoever adopts the middle way, they praise his ways and give him the tidings of deliverance,
but whoever goes right and left they vilify his ways and frighten him with ruin.
In this way, they served as lamps in these darknesses and guides through these doubts.

key_terms.أَيَّامِ اللَّهِ: Days of God (times of His favors/events)

ai.seo_question: How does divine remembrance purify the heart and guide believers during periods of prophetic absence?
ai.summary: This passage elucidates the metaphysical role of dhikr as a spiritual cleanser that restores sensory and cognitive clarity to the heart, a concept central to Shia gnosis (irfan). It highlights the continuity of divine guidance through the fatrah (periods between prophets), where chosen servants served as 'lamps' of truth, a theme that resonates with the Shia understanding of the Imams as the enduring proof of God during the Minor and Major Occultations.
